subject: series
synopsis: John Benson's long-running EC Comics fanzine and bibliographic journal — essential reference material for the history of EC Comics, combining scholarly analysis with deep affection for the source material.
author: John Benson

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's all-ages Star Wars anthology spanning all eras of the franchise with accessible stories designed to welcome younger readers to the universe. A consistently solid gateway series with clean art and straightforward adventure storytelling.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's all-ages Star Wars Adventures anthology series in its 2020 relaunch format, featuring short accessible stories from across the Star Wars timeline aimed at younger readers and families entering the franchise. A reliably fun entry point for new Star Wars comics readers.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Various mini-series following the X-Men's intergalactic space pirate allies led by Corsair, combining swashbuckling adventure with Marvel's cosmic mythology. The team's appeal translated inconsistently across different creative teams over multiple limited series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2007 anthology series offering standalone stories about Superman's early career by various creative teams, in the style of Batman: Legends of the Dark Knight. Featured notable arcs including Darwyn Cooke and Tim Sale's Kryptonite origin story, one of the finest Superman stories of the decade.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's reprints of Marvel's 1980s King Conan, Alan Zelenetz and Don Kraar's tales of Conan's reign over Aquilonia.
author: Alan Zelenetz, Don Kraar

subject: series
synopsis: Gilbert Shelton's beloved underground comix characters — Fat Freddy, Freewheelin' Franklin, and Phineas — and their anthropomorphic cat Fat Freddy's Cat, collected by Fantagraphics in new editions. One of the great ongoing comic strips of the underground era, celebrated for its anarchic drug-addled humor and Shelton's clear, expressive cartooning.
author: Gilbert Shelton

subject: series
synopsis: A British weekly anthology reprint comic published by Marvel UK, reprinting classic Hulk stories for British audiences alongside other Marvel content in the weekly format popular in the UK market.

subject: series
synopsis: Matthew Rosenberg's inventive 2021 DC mystery series in which the Joker hosts a puzzle-box whodunit involving the entire DC villain community, presenting clues and red herrings in a structure that rewards careful reading. A clever format that gave Rosenberg room to play with the Joker's narrator-as-unreliable-witness role.
author: Matthew Rosenberg

subject: series
synopsis: Eiji Otsuka and Housui Yamazaki's dark comedy-horror follows a group of Buddhist university students with supernatural abilities who deliver corpses to their requested final destinations. Sharp social commentary wrapped in macabre humor.
author: Eiji Otsuka

subject: series
synopsis: James Tynion IV and Isaac Goodhart's coming-of-age horror series about a teenage boy whose body harbors monstrous chaos.
author: James Tynion IV, Tate Brombal

subject: series
synopsis: Negi Haruba's popular romantic comedy follows a frugal genius student hired to tutor five identical quintuplet sisters who are all failing school. Known for its clever use of the mystery-format framing device revealing which sister he eventually marries.
author: Negi Haruba

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's 2021 series revisiting The Visitor — a key figure from the early Valiant mythology — with modern storytelling expanding his enigmatic origins.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Keith Giffen's 2013 DC series headlining Larfleeze and featuring various alien DC heroes including Caul (formerly Green Lantern), Blue Beetle, and others stranded on a galactic gladiatorial game show. A low-stakes but entertaining ensemble sci-fi adventure built around Giffen's irreverent sensibility and underused DC cosmic characters.
author: Keith Giffen

subject: series
synopsis: MAYBE's dark fantasy manga set after a civil war where soldiers were transformed into powerful monster-humans (Incarnates) to fight, and now must live with the consequences as one officer hunts his former comrades who've lost their humanity. A thoughtful exploration of the cost of war on those who survive it.
author: MAYBE

subject: series
synopsis: Sui Ishida's dark urban fantasy follows Kaneki Ken, a college student who becomes a half-ghoul after a near-fatal encounter and must navigate a secret society of flesh-eating beings hidden within Tokyo. Praised for its early psychological depth and striking artwork.
author: Sui Ishida

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's all-ages series about a boy who inherits a hyper-intelligent dog with psychic powers from his eccentric uncle. A gentle, lighthearted adventure series aimed at younger readers during the mid-1980s.
author: Lennie Herman, George Caragonne

subject: series
synopsis: Makoto Yukimura's sweeping historical epic begins as a brutal Viking revenge story before transforming into a profound meditation on pacifism and what it means to be truly free. Thorfinn's arc from violence-obsessed boy to a man seeking a land without war is one of manga's greatest character studies.
author: Makoto Yukimura

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Shooter and David Lapham's series for Shooter's short-lived Defiant Comics, featuring humans transplanted into a living alien world called Plasm that forms creatures and weapons from its own flesh. An ambitious world-building effort from Shooter's post-Valiant venture.
author: Jim Shooter

subject: series
synopsis: Gail Simone and Neil Googe's 2006 Wildstorm series: Sheriff Lindo investigates a murder in a retirement town for aging superheroes and villains.
author: Gail Simone

subject: series
synopsis: Kamome Shirahama's visually breathtaking fantasy follows young Coco, who discovers magic is written rather than innate and secretly begins to learn forbidden art. Celebrated for its extraordinarily detailed linework evoking classic European illustration and its thoughtful exploration of ability, disability, and institutional power.
author: Kamome Shirahama

subject: series
synopsis: A Wolverine tie-in to the Blood Hunt event exploring vampiric threats and the X-Men's involvement in the crisis.
author: Tom Waltz

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Latour's Infinite Comics digital series following Logan in Japan in a format designed for digital reading, significant as an early example of Marvel's digital-native storytelling experiments.
author: Jason Latour

subject: series
synopsis: Charlie Huston's explicit, controversial series featuring Wolverine fighting the sadistic Contagion in an ultra-violent, sexually charged style that divided critics, seen as excess without purpose.
author: Charlie Huston

subject: series
synopsis: Ed Brubaker's retroactive revelation of a secret third team of X-Men sent to Krakoa before the Giant-Size team, introducing Vulcan and upending the history of the X-Men with significant consequences for the Shi'ar space saga.
author: Ed Brubaker

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn's 2017 X-Men: Blue: the time-displaced original five X-Men, led by Jean Grey and mentored by Magneto.
author: Cullen Bunn, Steven T. Seagle

subject: series
synopsis: Marc Guggenheim's 2008 series following a new generation of young mutants recruited by Donald Pierce disguised as Cyclops, before the deception is revealed and the team must find its footing post-Messiah Complex. A short-lived but reasonably competent transitional X-Men series.
author: Marc Guggenheim

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison and Steve Yeowell's sophisticated 2000AD superhero series featuring a pop-star superhero entangled in Lovecraftian multiversal conspiracies; a landmark of British superhero deconstruction that prefigures Morrison's later DC work.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: A recent X-Men series examining the contest for Apocalypse's mantle and legacy among mutant candidates, playing on the enduring power of the En Sabah Nur mythology.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Bill Mantlo and Mike Mignola's 1985 miniseries establishing Rocket Raccoon's solo mythology on Halfworld, the asylum planet where he protected the inmates. Notable for Mignola's pre-Hellboy artwork and the character's foundational lore.
author: Bill Mantlo

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman's 2012 Avengers: Captain America and Iron Man expand the team to face the Builders, Infinity and the incursions leading to Secret Wars.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's 1985-1986 Captain Britain monthly: Jamie Delano and Alan Davis's Brian Braddock stories, with Night Raven and Abslom Daak backups.
author: Chris Claremont, Gary Friedrich

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Wagner's solo series. The original Claremont 4-issue mini is a charming swashbuckling adventure; the various ongoings are more variable.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2003 Silver Surfer series, viewing the Surfer through ordinary humans on Earth, cancelled after 14 issues.
author: Steve Englehart

subject: series
synopsis: Elaine Lee and Michael Kaluta's cult science fiction epic — a rich, dense, satirical space opera following a vast cast of colorful characters in a galaxy-spanning story that rewards patient, attentive reading.
author: Elaine Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Eric Powell's beloved black comedy horror series set in a depression-era city plagued by zombies, monsters, and crime — following the muscle-bound enforcer known as the Goon and his wise-cracking partner Franky as they battle the undead and the criminal underworld.
author: Eric Powell

subject: series
synopsis: Christian Gossett's creator-owned sci-fi/fantasy series set in a Russia-analog empire where magic and Soviet-era technology coexist. Distinguished by Gossett's striking hybrid digital-traditional art, it follows soldier Maya Antares amid a long-running war with devastating consequences.
author: Christian Gossett

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Snyder and Nick Dragotta's 2024 Absolute Batman: a Bruce Wayne without wealth or Alfred, a towering working-class brawler, wars on Gotham.
author: Bill Finger, George Shute

subject: series
synopsis: Collected Sergio Aragonés and Mark Evanier's Groo the Wanderer, the dim-witted barbarian who leaves disaster everywhere he goes.
author: Mark Evanier

subject: series
synopsis: The Rebirth Justice League (2016-2018): Bryan Hitch's blockbuster arcs, then Christopher Priest's acclaimed closing run.
author: Geoff Johns, Jeff Lemire

subject: series
synopsis: Rachel Pollack's 1995 New Gods: Orion and the Fourth World, leading into John Byrne's takeover.
author: Rachel Pollack, Mark Evanier

subject: series
synopsis: Rick Remender's 2009 Punisher: Frank Castle hunts the Hood, is killed by Daken and rebuilt as FrankenCastle.
author: Mike Baron

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Slott's 2024 Superior Spider-Man: Otto Octavius returns as the Superior Spider-Man in Supernova and Superior Spider-Island.
author: Dan Slott, Stephen Wacker

subject: series
synopsis: J. Michael Straczynski's acclaimed Thor relaunch, returning the Asgardians to Earth in a small Oklahoma town and rebuilding Thor's mythology with emotional depth, stunning Olivier Coipel art, and political intrigue.
author: J. Michael Straczynski

subject: series
synopsis: Charlie Huston and David Finch's brutal 2006 Moon Knight: a broken Marc Spector returns as Khonshu's fist, later Mike Benson's run.
author: Doug Moench, Charlie Huston

subject: series
synopsis: Wildstorm's 1996 Grifter ongoing: ex-Team 7 operative Cole Cash as a gun-for-hire, Steven T. Seagle scripting.
author: Steven T. Seagle, Steven Grant

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2015 Star Wars: Jason Aaron and John Cassaday's Luke, Leia and Han between A New Hope and Empire, later Kieron Gillen.
author: Jason Aaron, Greg Pak

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Lobdell's comedic 2004 Alpha Flight: Sasquatch recruits a mismatched new team to rescue the old one.

subject: series
synopsis: David Lapham's third Stray Bullets volume (2015-): Virginia, Beth, Orson and Spanish Scott's misadventures with Baltimore crime boss Harry.

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Orlando's 2022 Marauders: Kate Pryde's crew sails again as Krakoa's hunters of Hellfire threats.
author: Gerry Duggan

subject: series
synopsis: The annuals to Marvel's first Iron Man series (1970-1994), crossover tie-ins and extra stories.
author: Len Kaminski, Scott Benson

subject: series
author: Jude Ellison S. Doyle, Jordan Clark

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1975–1976 tryout anthology giving new characters and concepts a single issue to prove their worth, featuring Jack Kirby creating Atlas, Mike Grell introducing the Warlord (who got his own series), Steve Ditko's Manhunter, and others. An important artifact of DC's experimental mid-1970s period.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A What If...? miniseries imagining alternate scenarios in the Aliens franchise within the Marvel Comics licensing era, presenting divergent outcomes for the xenomorph encounters familiar from the film series.
author: Paul Reiser, Leon Reiser

subject: series
synopsis: Fabien Vehlmann and Bruno Gazzotti's Belgian survival thriller series following a group of children who wake up to find all adults have mysteriously vanished from the Earth. Vehlmann builds genuine dread and moral complexity into what could have been a simple Lord of the Flies riff, making the children's decisions feel consequential.
author: Fabien Vehlmann

subject: series
synopsis: The canonical comic continuation of the Buffy the Vampire Slayer TV universe, following Angel and Faith in London as they attempt to resurrect Giles — killed by Angel under Twilight's influence — while battling the fallout of magic's destruction.
author: Christos Gage

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning's sequel to Annihilation, featuring the Phalanx technological infection of the Kree Empire, and introducing the new Guardians of the Galaxy lineup that would star in their own series. Strong cosmic action.
author: Dan Abnett, Andy Lanning

subject: series
synopsis: Io Sakisaka's popular shojo romance follows Futaba who reunites with her middle school crush Kou years later only to find he's changed dramatically. Praised for its honest portrayal of teenage emotional complexity and character growth.
author: Io Sakisaka

subject: series
synopsis: The Geoff Johns New 52 launch is the definitive modern Aquaman — self-aware about the character's ridicule, then systematically dismantling it through strong storytelling. Dan Abnett's follow-up is also solid.
author: Paul Norris

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Duggan's 2014 series where Arkham Asylum is destroyed and Wayne Manor becomes Gotham's new facility for the criminally insane, with Bruce Wayne as a prisoner in disguise investigating murders.
author: Gerry Duggan

subject: series
synopsis: Original Valiant series featuring armored soldiers. Mid-tier Valiant action with the universe-building that made the original era compelling.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first vertical Infinity Comic featuring Spider-Man adventures formatted for mobile reading, delivering standalone action stories within the broader Spider-Man corner of the Marvel Universe.
author: Scott Aukerman

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Parker's crossover pairing the campy 1966 television Batman with the Cold War spy franchise The Man From U.N.C.L.E., perfectly capturing the period aesthetics and good-natured absurdity of both properties. A love letter to a specific moment in pop culture executed with great affection and comic timing.
author: Jeff Parker

subject: series
synopsis: Tom King and Clay Mann's prestige series resolving the romantic arc of Batman and Catwoman across multiple timelines.
author: Tom King

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Priest's 2022 series treating Teth-Adam as a genuine political figure rather than a simple villain — examining what an ancient Egyptian god-warrior with contempt for modern rules would actually do with power in the contemporary world. Priest's political acuity makes this one of the more thoughtful villain-as-protagonist comics DC has published.
author: Christopher Priest

subject: series
synopsis: Oversized editions of the acclaimed dimension-hopping sci-fi adventure about a rogue scientist's terrible mistake.
author: Rick Remender

subject: series
synopsis: Keiichi Arawi's slice-of-life comedy manga following the chaotic misadventures of broke student Midori Nagumo and her equally strange neighbors, colleagues, and acquaintances in a city where oddity is the norm. Arawi's comedic timing and ability to find warmth in absurdity make this a delightful follow-up to Nichijou.
author: Keiichi Arawi

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Millar and Steve McNiven's landmark event pitting Iron Man's pro-registration faction against Captain America's anti-registration heroes, a politically charged superhero war that defined Marvel's mid-2000s publishing strategy and remains one of its most culturally impactful events.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Jenkins's ground-level companion to Civil War following reporters Sally Floyd and Ben Urich covering the superhero war, adding human stakes to the blockbuster event through journalistic framing.
author: Paul Jenkins

subject: series
synopsis: DC's Golden Age anthology featuring Wonder Woman, The Flash, and Green Lantern adventures during comics' earliest era, documenting the original iterations of three of DC's most iconic heroes in accessible stories of their time.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's long Robert E. Howard adaptation. Roy Thomas's foundational scripts and Barry Windsor-Smith's early art are historically important. John Buscema defined the visual style of Conan for decades. Pulp fantasy at its most ambitious in comics form.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis's series following Norman Osborn's Dark Avengers — villains posing as heroes during the Dark Reign era — featuring a Thunderbolts-style examination of evil masquerading as good with strong art by Mike Deodato.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2014 digital-first Infinity Comic series featuring Deadpool on a globe-trotting mission that eventually becomes a tie-in to the Axis event, showcasing the format's ability to reveal information panel-by-panel in ways print cannot. Gerry Duggan's witty Deadpool voice was at its peak during this era.
author: Gerry Duggan, Brian Posehn

subject: series
synopsis: A high-achieving student discovers a supernatural notebook that kills anyone whose name he writes in it and begins using it to reshape the world as a self-appointed god of justice. Ohba and Obata's cat-and-mouse thriller is a masterclass in escalating intellectual tension.
author: Tsugumi Ohba

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's 1997 series following a hero from the future stranded in the present, continuing the Valiant universe mythology into the Acclaim Entertainment era. Part of the transition period when Valiant's core concepts were being reimagined under new corporate ownership.
author: Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: Titan Comics' second year of Tenth Doctor adventures featuring David Tennant's beloved incarnation in original comics stories that expand on the show's mythology with the Doctor and new companions.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Evan Dorkin's anthology comics collecting his strips including Milk and Cheese, the Eltingville Club, Bill and Ted material, and other humour and rants. Dorkin is one of the sharpest comedy writers in comics.
author: Evan Dorkin

subject: series
synopsis: J. Michael Straczynski and Sid Kotian's fantasy crime series following two detectives who police the world of dreams — ensuring that the dreaming realm doesn't bleed into reality.
author: J. Michael Straczynski

subject: series
synopsis: Italian anthology series from Bonelli Comics featuring full-color stories of Dylan Dog, the nightmare investigator who confronts monsters, zombies, and the supernatural horrors of London. Color Fest offered an international showcase for Dylan Dog to artists who don't normally work on Italian comics, giving the character unusual visual variety.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 anthology from the revived EC Comics label, collecting disturbing horror and sci-fi stories in the classic EC tradition of twist endings and social commentary. The new EC label's continuation of the original magazine's legacy of subversive genre storytelling.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1986 horror anthology series hosted by Elvira, Mistress of the Dark, mixing her trademark campy humor with actual horror short story comics from various creators. A fun curiosity that captured the cultural moment of Elvira's peak popularity.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse comics based on Sam Raimi's horror franchise. Ash Williams vs. deadites — captures the films' tone of splatstick horror comedy.
author: Mark Verheiden

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis' mind-bending sci-fi thriller about telepathic young adults in London.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's 2012 continuation of Snake Eyes: the silent commando and his rival Storm Shadow tangle with the Arashikage and Cobra.

subject: series
synopsis: Action comic adaptation based on the classic 1972 anime Battle of the Planets/Gatchaman, following the Science Ninja Team G-Force battling the terrorist organization Galactor.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Phil and Kaja Foglio's multiple Eisner Award-winning steampunk webcomic following Agatha Heterodyne, the heir to a dynasty of mad scientists, as she discovers her incredible powers and fights to reclaim her family's legacy in a Europe overrun by rampaging constructs and warring Sparks. Enormously entertaining with a complex world, great humor, and a genuinely brilliant protagonist.
author: Phil Foglio, Kaja Foglio

subject: series
synopsis: Antarctic Press's annual fan service publication collecting pinup art of Fred Perry's Gold Digger characters, primarily aimed at the series' established fanbase. A companion publication rather than a standalone series.
author: Fred Perry

subject: series
synopsis: Takao Saito's long-running (since 1968) manga features Duke Togo, the world's greatest assassin, completing contract killings with cold precision. One of the longest-running manga in history, an institution of the Japanese medium.
author: Takao Saito

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Tomasi's Guy Gardner series running alongside the main Green Lantern books during the Brightest Day era, sending Gardner on a secret mission into the Unknown Sectors. Tomasi writes Guy with the same gruff affection he'd shown in Corps.
author: Peter Tomasi

subject: series
synopsis: A deluxe hardcover edition of Geoff Johns's landmark Green Lantern: Rebirth miniseries that restored Hal Jordan as Green Lantern and redefined the character's mythology for a new generation.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Sebela and Ibrahim Moustafa's espionage thriller about a disgraced former Olympic skier-turned-Everest guide drawn into a conspiracy after discovering a body on the mountain. A tight, atmospheric crime story elevated by vivid mountain environment and strong character work.
author: Christopher Sebela

subject: series
synopsis: Takahiro and strelka's spinoff of Akame ga Kill follows Hinowa, a young warrior in a far eastern land inspired by feudal Japan fighting for freedom and survival. Shares the parent series' penchant for dramatic character deaths and action spectacle.
author: Takahiro

subject: series
synopsis: The Inhumans' first series (1975-1977): Doug Moench with George Pérez and Gil Kane, Black Bolt's royal family against Maximus and Kree threats.
author: Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: Jeremy Adams' 2023 limited series spotlighting Jay Garrick, the original golden-age Flash, as he returns to active duty in the modern DC universe. Adams applies the same warm, character-focused approach that distinguished his Barry Allen Flash run, giving Jay Garrick his most substantial contemporary showcase.
author: Jeremy Adams

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Jurgens's New 52 Justice League International: Booster Gold leads a UN-sponsored team of global heroes.
author: J. M. DeMatteis, Andrew Helfer

subject: series
synopsis: A quarterly anthology series featuring extended stories about the Justice League International and its various global branches. Focused on the Global Guardians and supporting characters from the Giffen/DeMatteis era.
author: Keith Giffen

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's eco-themed superhero series linking Arthurian mythology to environmental crises, with heroes channeling the spirit of the Round Table against corporate villains. A distinctly British take on superheroes that used genre conventions to argue for environmental activism.
author: Dan Abnett

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' comprehensive reprint of George Herriman's surrealist masterpiece Krazy Kat, a foundational work of American comics featuring a love triangle played out in the abstract landscape of Coconino County.
author: George Herriman

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Rucka and Michael Lark's dystopian series set in a near-future where the world is divided between powerful Families and their serfs; Forever Carlyle is the Lazarus — the genetically engineered warrior — of the Carlyle family, questioning her place in a brutal oligarchic world.
author: Greg Rucka

subject: series
synopsis: Si Spurrier's Krakoa-era X-Men series following Nightcrawler as the spiritual shepherd of mutantkind, running the Altar and policing the new mutant nation's borders between the physical and metaphysical. Spurrier's thoughtful exploration of faith, identity, and community gave it unusual depth.
author: Si Spurrier

subject: series
synopsis: Roman Dirge's dark-humor series about a cute dead little girl and the monsters, serial killers, and supernatural beings she encounters. Tim Burton-esque goth comedy with genuine affection for its morbid protagonists.
author: Roman Dirge

subject: series
synopsis: Al Ewing's clever, self-aware series about a younger Loki working for the All-Mother to rewrite his destiny, featuring sharp writing about identity, narrative, and the possibility of change for a character defined by treachery.
author: Al Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: Special issues of MAD Magazine published outside the regular schedule for seasonal or thematic content — Christmas issues, retrospectives, and one-theme compilations. Essential for MAD completists who appreciate the magazine's anarchic approach to political and pop culture satire.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A mid-2000s Fantastic Four title under the Marvel Knights banner, offering street-level adventures with the team stripped of their resources and status.
author: Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa, Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont's 2002 limited series following Kitty Pryde after she's lost her X-Men powers and is attending the University of Chicago, navigating a 'normal' college life while anti-mutant tensions escalate around her. A rare quiet Kitty Pryde story that treats her as a whole person beyond her powers.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Kieron Gillen and Omar Francia's sci-fi police procedural follows a law enforcement officer on Mercury — a story about a woman who can't be anywhere but the most inhospitable place, and what that says about her.
author: Kieron Gillen

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2017 event series and subsequent ongoing featuring Kid Kaiju, a young boy who can summon and create giant monsters, as he defends Earth from an invasion of massive alien creatures. A nostalgic celebration of Marvel's classic monster characters given a modern action-comedy framework.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Kazune Kawahara and Aruko's utterly charming shojo romance follows Takeo Gouda, a big scary-looking but gentle-hearted boy who always loses girls to his handsome best friend, until he meets Rinko who genuinely falls for him. A delightful subversion of shojo romance tropes.
author: Kazune Kawahara

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1991 infamously bad licensed comics series about a football player who becomes a superhero through an accident involving a special suit — created as a marketing vehicle and nearly universally agreed to be one of the worst superhero comics ever published. A fascinating low-water mark in mainstream comics.
author: Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' comics anthology edited by Eric Reynolds, spotlighting emerging and established alternative cartoonists from around the world with each issue. One of the best ongoing venues for discovering new voices in alternative and literary comics, carrying on the tradition of RAW and other great anthology series.
author: Various (Eric Reynolds, ed.)

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's 1990 solo Namor series, giving the Sub-Mariner his own dedicated ongoing for the first time since the golden age. Byrne restored Namor's regal dignity while building out his relationship with the business world above the surface.
author: Glenn Herdling

subject: series
synopsis: Masamune Shirow and Koushi Rikudou's sci-fi action manga set in a near-future featuring cyborg girls, a self-made island nation, and tech-comedy. More accessible and humorous than Shirow's Ghost in the Shell despite sharing the cyberpunk aesthetic.
author: Masamune Shirow, Koushi Rikudou

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1997 standalone Quicksilver series by John Ostrander, following Pietro Maximoff navigating his complicated relationships with the Avengers and Magneto while dealing with his own mercurial personality. A solid character examination for a hero whose inner life rarely gets dedicated attention.
author: John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Dave Gibbons' 2005 Infinite Crisis tie-in limited series depicting the war between the planet Rann (home of Adam Strange) and the bird-people of Thanagar (Hawkman's world), a cosmic conflict that set the stage for the larger Infinite Crisis event. A solid space-opera tie-in elevated by Gibbons' craft.
author: Dave Gibbons

subject: series
synopsis: Shawn Martinbrough and DC's 2024 series focusing on Jason Todd's Red Hood and his relationship with a Gotham neighborhood called the Hill, exploring community, identity, and the ethics of vigilantism from the perspective of a former villain trying to be a hero.
author: Shawn Martinbrough

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2024 Raven series bringing the empathic daughter of Trigon into a new contemporary story as she tries to build a life apart from her demonic heritage. Aimed at fans of the character from the Teen Titans animated series era.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Sebastian Girner and Galaad's light-hearted fantasy adventure following Luvander, a mysterious young woman with a secret, who joins a prince and his companions on a quest for legendary treasure.
author: Sebastian Girner

subject: series
synopsis: Nick Spencer's controversial event revealing Steve Rogers had been a Hydra sleeper agent due to Cosmic Cube manipulation, culminating in a Hydra takeover of America. Ambitious but divisive, particularly for its handling of Cap's character.
author: Nick Spencer

subject: series
synopsis: Todd DeZago's 1996 title replacing Web of Spider-Man as part of the Clone Saga era, and Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa's 2006 revival offering strong character-driven stories including a notable Doctor Strange team-up.
author: Todd DeZago

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2024 X-Men series from the From the Ashes era focusing on the Sentinel program — the mutant-hunting robots — and the human characters who operate and oppose them, examining the institutional mechanisms of anti-mutant discrimination rather than the mutants themselves.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1993 anthology series offering rotating spotlights on various DC characters — Catwoman, Cyborg, Blue Beetle, and others — in stories that often served as tryouts for potential ongoing series. A useful format for DC's period of post-Crisis character reinvention.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1995 anthology series continuing the tryout format from Showcase '93 and '94, featuring short stories spotlighting DC characters and concepts that hadn't yet found their own titles. An undervalued slice of mid-1990s DC's experimental output.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips's Wildstorm espionage noir follows Holden Carver, a deep-cover agent embedded in a supervillain organisation who can't break cover without exposing his handler. One of Brubaker and Phillips's finest collaborations, a relentlessly tense and morally corrosive thriller that asks whether there's any line between hero and villain when you live as both.
author: Ed Brubaker

subject: series
synopsis: Roger Langridge's charming all-ages adventure follows the Walrus and the Carpenter from Lewis Carroll's poem on a grand ocean adventure, with Langridge's characteristically witty writing and expressive art.
author: Roger Langridge

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2002 rebranding of the Cable series, following Nathan Summers after he was separated from the techno-organic virus that threatened his life, in a more globally-minded humanitarian direction. A transitional period for the character that didn't find a lasting direction.
author: Darko Macan

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's 1998 controversial retelling of Spider-Man's origin, updating the classic Stan Lee–Steve Ditko stories with modern references but fundamentally altering continuity in ways most fans rejected. An interesting experiment that remains a contested piece of Marvel history.
author: John Byrne

subject: series
synopsis: A spy, an assassin, and a telepath form a fake family — each hiding their true nature from the others — in a Cold War-inspired setting. Tatsuya Endo's manga is pure comedic delight with increasingly genuine emotional stakes between the characters.
author: Tatsuya Endo

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Gruenwald's 1985 maxi-series: the Squadron Supreme take over their America to build a utopia, and pay for it.
author: Mark Gruenwald, James Robinson

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue crossover limited series between the Star Trek (Kelvin timeline) and Green Lantern franchises, in which Power Ring wielders from the DC universe are transported to the Trek universe. Published by IDW with DC, written by Mike Johnson.
author: Mike Johnson

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's ongoing Star Trek comic set in the Kelvin Timeline following the 2009 film reboot — adapting and expanding stories for the Chris Pine/Zachary Quinto cast.
author: Mike Johnson

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Marvel miniseries set in the chaotic days immediately following the Battle of Endor, following New Republic forces and Imperial remnants clashing on Jakku as the empire crumbles.

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Marvel miniseries exploring the dark history of the Inquisitorius, Darth Vader's order of former Jedi turned Imperial hunters, set in the early years of the Empire.
author: Rodney Barnes

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Kelly and Chris Bachalo's WildStorm series featuring Cossack, a synthetic human who can manipulate time through an artifact called the Monstructor, stranded in a baroque alternate 19th-century England. Bachalo's art is characteristically hallucinatory and inventive, though the plot's complexity tested reader patience.
author: Joe Kelly

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2024 limited series adapting and expanding on the narrative logic of the Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League video game, sending the Squad into Arkham Asylum for a violent incursion mission. A straightforward action tie-in that delivers the pulpy violence its premise promises.
author: John Layman

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Venditti's continuation of his Superman '78 comics series, presenting new adventures of Christopher Reeve's cinematic Man of Steel in the aesthetic of the beloved 1978 film. A deeply affectionate tribute to the Reeve era that gives fans the 'extra' Superman movie they always wanted.
author: Robert Venditti

subject: series
synopsis: A horror-action series following Terror, a mercenary who can attach severed body parts to himself to gain their owner's skills and memories, in a darkly comedic noir setting.
author: D.G. Chichester

subject: series
synopsis: Collected archive editions of Red Sonja's classic adventures — the She-Devil with a Sword fighting through the Hyborian Age in the Marvel/Dynamite run, across multiple eras of the character's publication history.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2014 digital Infinity Comic featuring Spider-Man in a mystery about identity and memory, produced for the infinite-canvas vertical format of digital delivery. A solid Infinity Comics entry from Marvel's early push into digital-first content.
author: Joshua Hale Fialkov

subject: series
synopsis: WildStorm's 2001 series by Charlie Adlard and Ian Edginton following a black-ops team of strange metahumans serving British intelligence, a WildStorm analog to Britain's more sinister answers to The Authority. Part of WildStorm's interconnected superhero universe with a distinctly British espionage flavor.
author: Ian Edginton

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue Countdown to Infinite Crisis miniseries in which Batman's Brother Eye satellite is revealed to have gone rogue, converting humans into OMACs to hunt metahumans.
author: Greg Rucka

subject: series
synopsis: Brian K. Vaughan and Marcos Martin's brilliant digital-first noir set in a future where the internet has collapsed and privacy is currency. Originally published pay-what-you-want. Martin's art is some of his finest work; the premise is prophetically sharp.
author: Brian K. Vaughan

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn and Brian Hurtt's supernatural western: Becky Montcrief inherits one of six cursed guns and is hunted by the undead General Hume.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning's cosmic capstone to their Marvel space saga, featuring Thanos as the instrument of Death against the Cancerverse, culminating in the sacrifice of Nova and Star-Lord. A fitting conclusion to one of Marvel's best cosmic runs.
author: Dan Abnett, Andy Lanning

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Jurgens's sequel to his original Time Masters limited series, following Rip Hunter's attempts to find Batman after Final Crisis while establishing the history of Booster Gold's timeline manipulation.
author: Dan Jurgens

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore's ABC anthology of short strips: Greyshirt, Jack B. Quick, Cobweb, Splash Brannigan and The First American.
author: Alan Moore

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's TPB collections adapting the acclaimed Transformers Animated animated series (2007–2009), which reimagined the Transformers as a younger, more adventurous Autobot crew with a distinctive anime-influenced art style. A well-crafted all-ages adaptation of a show that earned unusual critical respect.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Budjette Tan and Kajo Baldisimo's acclaimed Filipino supernatural detective series following Alexandra Trese, a criminal investigator who operates in the shadow world of Philippine mythology and folklore beneath the streets of Manila. One of the most distinctive comics from Southeast Asia — rich in cultural specificity, genuinely thrilling as crime fiction, and beautifully illustrated.
author: Budjette Tan
